newsitem.title: FRANCE: French civil service unions consider March strike.
newsitem.headline: French civil service unions consider March strike.

text.p: French civil service trade unions are considering calling a strike in March in their campaign to win a better pay award after a wage freeze in 1996, CGC civil service union leader Pierre Avignon said on Wednesday.
Avignon said civil service minister Dominique Perben was due to announce government pay proposals on Tuesday but that they were expected to fall short of union demands.
"We (the unions) have decided to meet that evening and, possibly, announce a strike call," Avignon, the secretary general of the CGC's civil service branch, told Reuters.
Unofficial contacts with the ministry in the past few days led unions to believe that Perben was not willing to make any concessions on a "catch-up" in salaries for 1996, he said.
"We're expecting the government's proposals on February 4. It appears now that they won't live up to what we want," he said.

Avignon said the main unions involved were seeking pay rises of 1.4 percent in 1997 and the same in 1998 and were also looking for at least a gesture from the ministry to make up for the loss of purchasing power in 1996.
The CGC and other unions wanted to negotiate but some of the unions were taking a harder line, he said.
Avignon said unions planned to meet in the evening after Perben's announcement to decide their course of action.
If a strike were to be called, school holidays in February as well as the need to organise would make March the "logical choice" for action, he said.

State teachers and other civil servants went on strike for a day on October 17 to protest against government plans to trim the civil service by around 6,000 in 1997 and to demand the opening of wage negotiations.
The turnout was relatively modest. Perben said that about one in three civil servants joined the strike.
The renewal of tensions in the civil service comes at a time when the government also faces protest from railway and public transport workers.

SNCF state railway workers start a 36-hour strike over rail reform at 1900 GMT today and two unions have called for another one day regional transport strike on February 5 following a well-supported one-day stoppage on Friday to press for a cut in work time and earlier retirement.
